i

R E A L I ZA T I O N  C AL C U L U S
SCOPE
ii
S C O P E
Objects, operators and arithmetic
Realization Calculus studies how mathematical objects are generated from seeds, resolved into
packets and related by operators. The twelve core papers develop this language across linear
and nonlinear constructions, signal analysis, dynamics and arithmetic.
Projectors specify the components retained in a description. Transfer records the action between
components and the passage from one resolution to another. The resulting questions concern
reconstruction, compatibility, analytic control and the additional structure required for a
realization.
Each result is read with its stated hypotheses. Finite identities, analytic arguments and
arithmetic constructions occupy different settings. The visual studies illustrate selected
examples, while the formal companions identify the precise declarations and assumptions
covered by their mathematical interfaces.
The final arithmetic realization theorems depend on specified inputs. Conjecture 66 in Paper XI
remains open. Paper XII requires suitable residual and deformation data, patching and full
support, a Hecke point over the same coefficient field with the required compatibility,
classicality and an attached representation. The existence of these inputs is not a universal
conclusion of the paper.
The collection presents the core sequence as a connected course of study. Its scope is the
mathematics of these twelve papers, with the boundaries of each construction stated where they
are used.

R E A L I ZA T I O N  C AL C U L U S
INTRODUCTION
iii
I N T R O D U C T I O N
A route through the calculus
A choice of resolution determines which components of an object are visible and how their
interactions are represented. Across these papers, seed constructions, projectors and packet
coordinates organize this passage between an object and its descriptions.
Three questions recur. Which objects can be generated from the available seeds? Which relations
survive a change of resolution? What further hypotheses permit a compatible description to be
realized in the intended analytic or arithmetic setting?
The Projector Resolved Seed Calculus establishes the initial constructions. The later papers
develop multiresolution signal methods, transfer semigroups and memory, quantum dynamics,
and packet operator algorithms. The final arithmetic treatments examine congruences, residual
seeds, packet geometry and patching support.
The mathematical treatment in each part gives the principal argument. Visual studies supply
examples and geometric interpretations. Formal and verification companions provide a route to
exact hypotheses, source correspondences and the limits of formal coverage.
The papers may be read in sequence or approached through a particular construction. Part
openings identify the constituent treatments and their scope. The contents and bookmarks
connect these local routes to the whole collection.

method.text: All displayed pages normalized by NFKC, casefold, alphabetic characters only.
method.raw_sources: Every raw build hash is checked against component_builds.json; 35 unaffected components must be byte-identical.
method.edited_sources: All 154 pages in six adapted components compared against raw PDFs. Every nonbranding nonspace glyph and position must agree. Page-pair RGB pixels at 72dpi are compared outside independently derived old/new label bands plus two-pixel antialias margins. Deviations remain explicit: at most two pixels with channel delta at most3 can be classified as a warning only if all vector structures/styles agree within0.0001 and 144/288dpi pixels are exact outside the same bands. Larger or unexplained changes fail.
method.limitations: Raster preservation is 72dpi; exact glyph geometry complements it. Frozen attachment hashes are independently checked by audit_monograph.py. This is an editorial preservation audit, not a mathematical or formal proof audit.
